text:
ellie: quick one — PR #4123 (migration guide) is blocked: docs preview failed and GH says required checks not satisfied. need input: wait for the preview fix or relax autopilot rules?

sam: what failed in the preview? is it a rendering error or the CI job timed out?

docs-preview-bot: Preview build started: https://preview.redwood.example/pr/4123 status: FAILED
logs: 
```
Error: jekyll-build: plugin "redwood-docs-extensions" failed at asset-compile step
Task timed out after 10m
```

max: that's the plugin we've seen flake on bigger migration pages. it's not a content problem, it's infra.

ellie: right — content is fine (I checked locally). but branch protection requires "docs/preview" check to pass before you can merge.

tara: can we mark the preview check as optional for docs-only changes? that'd let CODEOWNERS approvals and other checks gate merge without the preview.

jess: cautious about that — we lose the safety net for formatting/regressions. maybe make it optional only for changes under /docs/reference/* and /docs/migrations/* where we know plugin churn is common.

sam: techncially GH branch protections allow required checks list to be toggled. Another option: add an "allow-failing: docs-preview" label that a repo-admin can apply to bypass the check for this PR.

max: +1 for scoped rule. also, we should avoid manual labels if we can automate. e.g., a small GitHub Action that detects only markdown changes and flips the docs-preview check to non-blocking by posting a status context.

ellie: I sketched a CODEOWNERS + branch rule approach last week. idea: CODEOWNERS requests docs-team reviewers automatically; branch protection requires approvals and CI but makes docs-preview optional for "docs-only" changes via a short action. thoughts?

tara: that seems reasonable. Do we have a prototype action?

sam: there's a simple action snippet used elsewhere. gist: 
```
# .github/workflows/docs-preview-bypass.yml (concept)
on: pull_request
n
jobs:
  detect-docs-only:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: detect changed paths
        run: |
          git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin ${{ github.base_ref }}
          echo "CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only origin/${{ github.base_ref }}...HEAD | grep -E '^docs/|^content/|\.md$' || true)" >> $GITHUB_ENV
      - name: set status
        if: env.CHANGED != '' && env.CHANGED == github.sha
        run: |
          # post a non-blocking status or add a label to indicate docs-only
          echo "posting status: docs-only"
```

jess: small detail: GH Actions can't flip branch protection; but they can post a status context that branch protection can use if configured. or they can add a label which an admin-level action interprets.

ellie: ok. For this specific PR, can someone with admin rights add label `docs:infra-flake` so we can merge after CODEOWNERS approvals? I'm fine if we tighten rules after we roll a reliable action.

max: I can add the label. tagging @sam for admin merge after approvals.

sam: I don't have admin on that repo — @tara can you add the label and merge once docs-team approves?

tara: done — added label `docs:infra-flake`. also updated the PR comment with the failing log.

ellie: thanks. small follow-up: we should update CODEOWNERS to explicitly include `/docs/migrations/` so PRs like this auto-request the right reviewers. can someone open a tiny PR to the repo?

jess: I'll open a CODEOWNERS tweak PR and include a short note about the planned action. will ping infra for permission model around the label-based bypass.

docs-preview-bot: New preview attempt queued by @tara: https://preview.redwood.example/pr/4123 (status: PENDING)

max: if the retry fails again, we merge with the label. we need a retro to harden the plugin.

ellie: agreed. thanks all — keeping this thread for the post-merge checklist. :thumbsup:
